_description: Parts catalog for the Claudia build. Each part has a 'searchFor' Google Shopping URL plus at least 3 direct tier links (amazon -> official -> reputable). Prices are NON-AUTHORITATIVE estimates - they go stale fast. Refresh by querying current Google Shopping results (per part) and updating both 'price' (USD, integer dollars) and 'pricesAsOf' (date last verified, top-level).
_configAxesNote: The build options the README describes (its build-options and parts tables are written by hand from this file). Each part's `when` field gates it to an axis value; 'default' is the option the README marks as default. Keys/values MUST agree with the part `when` gates and the README (CLA-LAW-4): battery=no|yes, mic=basic|array, asr=vosk|openai, tts=piper|openai|elevenlabs, case=none|fdm|sla, smarthome=none|kasa|shelly|sonoff. asr/tts values are upstream ASR_SERVER/TTS_SERVER names (elevenlabs only after the guide's patch); local options are the defaults (CLA-LAW-1).

categories.core: Required for every build. The Pi Zero 2 WH has no audio jack, so the USB speaker is what Claudia talks through.
categories.mic: The conversation microphone — required, pick one. The WonderEcho only handles the wake word; it never streams audio to the Pi.
categories.portable: Optional battery for a roaming build.
categories.smarthome: Optional locally-controllable smart plugs. Lets Claudia run commands like 'Claudia turn on the living room' without any cloud round-trip beyond Claude itself.

parts.name: Raspberry Pi Zero 2 WH
parts.note: Must be the WH (with pre-soldered headers). The plain W has no GPIO pins and would need 40 pins soldered before the WonderEcho's 4-pin cable can connect. Most retailers list WH as a dropdown variant of the W product page — pick 'with headers' before adding to cart. Supply is intermittent — if all US retailers show out-of-stock, rpilocator.com tracks live availability.

parts.name: Seeed reSpeaker XVF3800 USB 4-Mic Array (far-field upgrade)
parts.note: The higher-quality alternative to the SunFounder mini mic: four MEMS mics with on-chip XMOS DSP (echo cancellation, beamforming, neural noise suppression, dereverberation) for 360° pickup up to ~5 m — Alexa-grade far-field capture. Standard USB Audio Class 2.0, so it's driverless ALSA just like the basic mic. It also has a speaker output (3.5 mm jack + JST connector), so a powered or small passive speaker on the array can replace the USB speaker and hub; the guide's default is still the USB speaker.

parts.name: micro-USB OTG hub, 3-4 port, USB-only (no Ethernet)
parts.note: Required — the Pi Zero 2 WH has a single USB data port and no audio jack, and the build needs two USB devices on it: the conversation mic and the USB speaker. Plug the hub into the MIDDLE port labeled 'USB' (the data/OTG port), never the corner 'PWR IN' port, which carries power only. Any bus-powered USB 2.0 hub with a micro-B OTG plug works. Skip hub+Ethernet combos: their network chip draws ~280 mA even when unused (The Pi Hut's figure).

parts.name: TP-Link Kasa HS103 / KP125M smart plug (local control via python-kasa)
parts.note: Works locally over the LAN with the python-kasa library — no cloud round-trip at switch time. Tell Claudia 'turn on the living room' and a one-line shell call flips it. Caveat: the KP125M and HS103s on newer firmware use TP-Link's authenticated local protocol (KLAP), which needs your TP-Link account email and password once for the local handshake, so they are not account-free. Older-firmware HS103s are.

specs.value: HS103 (single) / HS103P2 (2-pack). KP125M is the newer Matter-capable equivalent and also works with python-kasa.

parts.name: Hiwonder WonderEcho voice module (I2C wake-word frontend)
parts.note: The hardware wake-word trigger — NOT the conversation microphone. Its CI1302 chip recognizes the wake word on-device and reports a result byte over I²C; it never streams raw audio, so the build also needs the USB mic above. 'Claudia' is taught to it once by voice (factory firmware: say 'Hello Hiwonder', then 'study wake', then the new word). Power it from the Pi's 5 V pin; the vendor says to use 5 V to avoid damage. Does not include any wiring — connect it to the Pi's GPIO header with 4 female-to-female jumper wires (see the ELEGOO Dupont kit below).

parts.name: ELEGOO 120pcs Dupont Jumper Wire Kit (M-F / M-M / F-F)
parts.note: Required. The WonderEcho does not include any wiring, so you need these to tie the wake-word module to the Pi's GPIO header. This 120-pc assortment gives you the female-to-female wires for the 4-pin link (SDA → pin 3, SCL → pin 5, 5V → pin 2, GND → pin 6) plus jumpers for any other GPIO wiring. 2.54 mm pitch matches the Pi Zero 2 WH header exactly.
